messages:
Linh: FYI ran a layout sweep on the KV-cache shaping + kernel autopicker last night. Found a weird perf cliff at seq_len ~512 for MQA when using split-page layout.
Samir: ugh cliff meaning latency spike or throughput drop?
Linh: 1.3x latency at tail for 512-640 ranges (p99). Throughput drops ~20% for small batch sizes.
Tara: can you paste the perf numbers and config?
Linh: sure — baseline: contiguous KV layout + default kernel picker. sweep: split-page layout with 128B block granularity, prefetch on, kernel_autopick=on.
Linh: perf-bot: results below
perf-bot: [AUTOMATED BENCH] model=redwood-open-gqa, hw=A100-80GB, bs=4, seq=256 -> qps=4200, p50=12ms, p99=28ms
perf-bot: [AUTOMATED BENCH] model=redwood-open-mqa, hw=A100-80GB, bs=4, seq=512 -> qps=3100, p50=18ms, p99=64ms :rotating_light:
Jess: that's a big p99 jump. Is kernel selector picking a paged-attn path?
Linh: yes. Kernel picker favored paged-attn-kvblock for many MQA shards because of cache miss patterns. For GQA it stayed on unified-attn for these sizes.
Miguel: hypothesis: per-head KV cache packing across MQA shards increases random accesses, so paged kernels suffer from stripe misalignment at 128B block size. Could be prefetch policy not covering the tail.
Samir: can we try 256B blocks or increase prefetch window?
Linh: did that. With block_size=256 and prefetch=2 pages we get p99 34ms and qps up ~12% vs 128B. Not quite baseline but much better.
Tara: interesting. Any memory overhead?
Linh: +8% GPU mem for block_size 256 (more wasted per block) but within Dedicated footprint we can accept it.
Jess: what about fallback: if seq_len between [480,700] force unified-attn kernel for MQA?
Samir: forcing solved p99 but reduced qps at seq=256 for MQA by ~6% (since unified path is heavier at shorter lengths). It's a tradeoff.
Miguel: propose adaptive rule: kernel_autopick uses a latency model with two dims: seq_len and shards_per_token. If predicted p99 > threshold for picked kernel, switch to alternate kernel. Keep a hysteresis window to avoid flapping.
Linh: drafted simple rule in runtime cfg:
```
kernel_autopick: on
rules:
  - name: mqa_paged_fallback
    if: "model_sharding == 'MQA' and seq_len >= 480 and seq_len <= 700 and batch_size <= 8"
    prefer: unified_attn
    hysteresis_ms: 30
```
Samir: looks good. We should train the latency predictor with the new features: block_size, prefetch_pages, shards_per_token.
perf-bot: scheduled retrain for latency-model job 1865432115 -> queued
Linh: also filed a small regression alert so ops-bot can route traffic if experiment trips SLOs.
ops-bot: [ALERT ROUTE] experiment "split-page-sweep-2026-03-17" will autoscale to Dedicated fallback on p99 breach > 50ms for 5m.
Tara: next steps: 1) add block_size and prefetch to autotune grid, 2) retrain latency model, 3) implement adaptive rule with hysteresis, 4) run A/B on small traffic.
Miguel: I'll run the grid with 64/128/256/512 block sizes + prefetch 0/1/2, on both GQA and MQA configs.
Linh: thanks. I'll instrument extra KV-cache hit counters and per-kernel stall counters to help the model features.
Jess: can you log an example of headers we want? Suggest: `kv_block_hits`, `kv_block_misses`, `prefetch_success`, `kernel_choice` per request.
Linh: on it. I'll post the trace example later.
Samir: nice find. This explains a recent customer micro-regression we saw on Dedicated with mixed MQA traffic. Good path forward.
Miguel: ETA for results?
Linh: 24-36h for grid + retrain, then can schedule canary.
Tara: cheers — call out if you want me to pause rollout. :thumbsup:
